name: Pradeep Biswal
intro: A poet in Odia and English, a translator and an editor, Pradeep Biswal brings a life in literature and public service to Kabita Live.
summary: Poetry, translation and the conversation between languages.

sections.heading: Words that cross between languages.
paragraphs: Pradeep Biswal writes poetry in both Odia and English. His literary work also includes translation and editing, and his poems have travelled into other Indian languages. At Kabita Live, where he is listed as Editor, that bilingual practice sits naturally within a journal that welcomes Odia, Hindi and English together.

His Odia collections include Bhumiparasha, Dhusara Dhrupadi, Seshaloka, Prema Kavita and Pheriba Batare. Setu’s author profile also records Jal Darpan and Lautte Raste Mein, two collections of his poetry in Hindi translation. These books offer several paths into his writing, through the original language and through the work of translation.

sections.heading: The inward house, the world outside.
paragraphs: A House Within, published by Authorspress in 2018, is an English collection that offers a useful starting point. In his review, Bhaskaranand Jha Bhaskar discusses its attention to nature, love, introspection and social concerns. The book’s title becomes a way of thinking about inward life: the feelings and contradictions that remain within the places we inhabit.

The review also describes a poetry alert to the public world, including war, hardship and the lives of ordinary people. Its account presents contemplation and social observation as neighbouring concerns, rather than separate compartments of the poet’s work.

sections.heading: A life in words and public service.
paragraphs: Alongside his literary career, Biswal served in the Indian Administrative Service. His own biographical note records his retirement as Special Secretary in Odisha’s Finance Department. Poetry, translation and editorial work form the continuing literary thread through that public-service background.

sources.label: Bhaskaranand Jha Bhaskar · Review of A House Within, 2019

name: Paresh Kumar Pattnaik
intro: An Odia fiction writer whose work includes short stories, novels and books for younger readers, Paresh Kumar Pattnaik is Kabita Live’s Managing Editor.
summary: Stories, social observation and an invitation to younger readers.

sections.heading: A storyteller’s way of seeing.
paragraphs: Paresh Kumar Pattnaik writes fiction in Odia and is listed by Kabita Live as its Managing Editor. Literary-festival and publisher profiles also use the spelling Paresh Kumar Patnaik. His work moves between the short story, the novel and writing for younger readers.

Puri Literature Festival’s profile describes a storyteller who approaches social questions through humour and compassion. It highlights his questioning of superstition and religious fanaticism, and records an Odisha Sahitya Akademi award for his work as a novelist. This is a literary practice concerned with how people live together, as well as how a story is told.

sections.heading: Many forms of a story.
paragraphs: His novels include Shoka Divas, Katha Thila and Seshara Arambha. Among his short-story collections are Iswar Aniswar, Abasistansha, Bhasi Jaa Mora Kagaj Danga, Swan Brutanta and Hrudayahin. The festival profile also notes that his stories have reached readers through translations into English, Hindi and other Indian languages.

sections.heading: Room for the younger reader.
paragraphs: Shalandi’s author catalogue makes another part of his range visible: children’s and young readers’ books alongside fiction for adults. It lists Musa O Musi, Goindagiri, Chor Police, Chori Bahir Rahasya, Nadiabari Bhut and Bhutar Bhet, as well as titles such as School re Chori and Nila Shirt Ra Rahasya.

For a reader meeting his work for the first time, this range offers several starting points: a novel, a collection of short stories or a book to share with a younger reader. The selected titles below link to the publisher’s listings, while the festival biography offers a wider introduction to his literary work.
